evidence.ready_list_ab_vs_sn_oracle: textbin/fun_00201128 sched2 ready lists: with P26/P33 only cycles t=6 and t=7 differ from the SN 2.95.2 oracle (ours issues the $ra save 100 with moves 10/12 still pending; SN issues the capture move). Without P26/P33 all 38 cycles are identical (dumps-p36/).
evidence.why_pairwise_rules_failed: The comparator is not a total order: qsort compares only some pairs, and the ra save is never compared with the deciding capture moves (10/12), so pairwise $ra-vs-move predicates (P36 fanout discount, P44, P45) could not act. The order was established transitively through the frame stores, which the blanket preference promoted.
evidence.causal_chain: P26 promoted non-$ra frame stores (106/104) over the capture moves (depend_count would prefer the moves, 9 vs 8 forward deps), and transitivity then placed the $ra save (100) at the tail.

mechanism: gcc/haifa-sched.c rank_for_schedule(): delete the frame-related-store preference block that compared frame stores against non-frame instructions (with P33's $ra exception). Scheduling then follows the untouched upstream chain (priority, last-scheduled class, depend_count, LUID), which is what retail keeps for textbin/fun_00201128's prologue and for the six former P26 fixtures.
stack_effect: P26 and P33 remain in the published stack history; 0036 neutralizes their block so the cumulative stack keeps a single deterministic build.
role: Retire the P26/P33 frame-store preference in rank_for_schedule. The preference is no longer needed to match retail after P29's call-clobber graph: all six P26 conversions stay exact without it, and removing it fixes the last blocked $ra-placement residual.
